Now that Trump has said that NATO is obsolete, it would seem a good idea to me for the various European nations to regionally reconsider their safety and the geopolitical role they would be willing and desiring to play on the world stage. Two layers of reality should be taken into account here:

  • the material layer: practical matters, like geography, logistics, economy etc.
  • the spiritual layer: socio-cultural aspects, like history, linguistic, religion etc.

With that in mind, it would seem logical to me that the North Sea countries form some sort of league within NATO.

The following is of course nothing more than an exercise in alternative history, but imho it can't hurt to share such ideas.

Let's consider 4 categories of 'membership' for the assumed League, which decides how many delegates they will in the Security Council, and also the extent to which these members contribute.

   

Membership Category I:

  • The United Kingdom

Because of its size (about 64 million inhabitants), because of its politics (Brexit) and military expenses, the UK deserves its own category.

The UK has twelve delegates in the Council. (In case of a UK split-up: eight delegates for England, three for Scotland, and one for Wales which would become a Category III country.)

   

Membership Category II: The other North Sea states

 

Membership Category II.a: North Sea states which are part of the Euro zone

  • The Netherlands

  • Belgium

 

Membership Category II.b: North Sea states which are not part of the Euro zone

  • Danmark

  • Norway

  • Iceland

  • Faroe Islands (actually, an autonomous region of Denmark, but in this context regarded an independent state)

Membership Category II nations each have three delegates in the council.

   

Membership Category III: States with no North Sea shore, but closely associated:

  • Luxembourg

  • Ireland

  • Sweden

These states each have one delegate in the council.

   

Membership Category IV: Regions of Germany and France with a North Sea shore:

  • Hauts-de-France

  • Schleswig-Holstein

  • Niedersachsen (Lower Saxony)

  • Freie Hansestadt Bremen (Free Hanseatic City of Bremen)

These regions each have one delegate in the council.

   

Only Category I and II members are considered full members; category III and IV have an observer status.
